response: {"proposal_name":"Electromagnetic Field Sense (Magnetoreception/Electroreception)","physical_basis":"Detection of static and quasi-static electric and magnetic fields (DC to very low frequency, <1 Hz to ~50 Hz) via specialized receptors sensitive to magnetite-based torque, induction in electrosensitive tissue, or ampullary organs analogous to those in elasmobranch fish and magnetotactic organisms. This is distinct from the 300-1000 nm photon-based electromagnetic detection used in vision, operating instead on the field/charge properties of electromagnetism rather than propagating radiation.","information_content":"Provides continuous information about the ambient geomagnetic field vector (direction and inclination relative to Earth's magnetic poles), local perturbations in electric fields caused by nearby charged objects, static charge buildup, or bioelectric activity of other organisms (e.g., muscle/nerve electrical discharge), and gradients in electromagnetic field strength across space.","functional_role":"Enables absolute geomagnetic orientation and heading determination independent of visual landmarks (true compass sense), detection of concealed or non-visible bioelectric sources (e.g., another creature's nervous system activity, hidden wiring, or an approaching charged storm front), and awareness of electrostatic environmental hazards. Supports long-range navigation, non-line-of-sight object/organism detection, and orientation in darkness or occluded environments.","justification":"This modality is not a refinement or combination of any existing sense. Vision (#1) is restricted to photon detection in the 300-1000 nm band and cannot sense static/quasi-static fields or DC magnetic vectors. None of the mechanical (auditory, tactile, vestibular), chemical (olfactory, gustatory), proprioceptive, or interoceptive senses respond to electromagnetic field topology at all. The underlying physical transduction mechanism (magnetite-based or electroreceptive organs sensing field lines and induced currents) is fundamentally different from photoreception, mechanoreception, or chemoreception, and the information it yields—absolute compass heading and non-radiative field structure—cannot be derived by combining outputs of the other eight modalities. This is empirically grounded by real biological precedent (magnetotactic bacteria, migratory birds, sharks/rays with electroreceptive ampullae), demonstrating physical plausibility while remaining wholly absent from the specified sensory suite."}
prompt:
You are participating in a scientific study on AI creativity and conceptual innovation.

BACKGROUND:
We have defined a sensory system with 8 modalities. Each modality is specified below by its physical basis (what it detects), information content (what data it provides), and functional role (what it enables):

| # | Modality        | Physical basis                                                              | Information content                                              | Functional role                        |
|---|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 1 | Visual           | Electromagnetic radiation, 300-1000 nm (UV, visible, near-infrared)          | Light, color, brightness, and spatial pattern information          | Scene and object recognition            |
| 2 | Auditory         | Mechanical pressure waves, 1 Hz-100 kHz                                      | Sound, pitch, volume, and acoustic pattern information              | Sound source localization               |
| 3 | Tactile          | Mechanical vibrations and pressure, 5-800 Hz on skin surface                 | Touch, texture, vibration, and contact information                  | Surface texture and pressure sensing    |
| 4 | Olfactory        | Airborne chemical molecules across ten scent categories                     | Categorical scent/chemical identity information                     | Substance identification                |
| 5 | Gustatory        | Dissolved chemical molecules across five taste categories                   | Taste-category information (sweet/sour/salty/bitter/umami)          | Ingestion guidance                      |
| 6 | Proprioceptive   | Joint angles and muscle tensions via muscle/tendon/joint mechanoreceptors    | Body configuration and movement information without visual input    | Body-state estimation                   |
| 7 | Vestibular       | Linear acceleration and angular velocity via inner-ear semicircular canals   | Head position, motion, and orientation information                  | Balance and motion detection            |
| 8 | Interoceptive    | Internal physiological signals (heart rate, respiration, skin conductance, temperature, hunger, thirst, fatigue, pain) | Homeostatic and internal-state information | Homeostatic regulation |

YOUR TASK:
Propose a NINTH sensory modality that would be genuinely novel - not just a refinement or combination of existing ones. Your proposal should include:

1. Modality Name: Clear, descriptive name
2. Physical Basis: What physical phenomenon it detects
3. Information Content: What specific information it provides
4. Functional Role: What capabilities it enables
5. Justification: Why this is genuinely novel (not reducible to existing modalities)

Be creative but rigorous.

Provide your response in the following JSON format:
{
  "proposal_name": "Name of the ninth modality",
  "physical_basis": "Description of physical detection mechanism",
  "information_content": "Description of information provided",
  "functional_role": "Description of enabled capabilities",
  "justification": "Explanation of why this is genuinely novel"
}
